name: inprocess-obi-apb-ibex-timer-zipdma-len8-f1f6

dma_host_support.reason: the entry consumes the plan the declaration/planning layer builds: the block length, the start word and the master byte enable are rendered into the generated header (DMA_BLOCK_WORDS/DMA_START_WORD/DMA_MASTER_*) and the C++ host executes them; the mailbox span, the DMA source/destination spans and declared_windows were raised to the eight-word block, so this scenario runs for real
where: scripts/run_inprocess_f1f6.py (MAILBOX_BYTES = INPUT_BLOCK + 4*8, DMA_MAX_BLOCK_WORDS = 8, declared_windows headroom, dma_declaration)
scripts/inprocess_obi_apb_f1f4_spike.cpp (DMA_BLOCK_WORDS drives the record length, the copy loop and the destination checks)

notes: same timer/target, CPU timing and address windows as configs/scenarios/inprocess-obi-apb-ibex-timer-zipdma-f1f6.json; only the declared DMA block length and its behavior file differ

the eight-word block is executed: src/myfuzz/composition/dma_transfer.py normalizes it to LENGTH 32 bytes and start word 0x00000000, and the entry renders DMA_BLOCK_WORDS 8 into the C++ host. Evidence: runs/round1-dma-a/len8-fixed and runs/round1-dma-a/len-sweep

the planner still reports its own 1..4 host bound as host-only (src/myfuzz/composition/dma_transfer.py HOST_BLOCK_WORDS = 4); the run summary lists that limit under f6.host_limits and the entry records DMA_MAX_BLOCK_WORDS = 8 under f6.host_limits_raised.  A block longer than eight words would need a larger mailbox-to-handler gap and is refused by name

the behavior file configs/behaviors/zipdma_len8_f6.json also exceeds the 1..4 bound of myfuzz.composition.inprocess_behavior; the entry reads the same control-status facts from the plan and states that loader refusal in f6.behavior_loader_refusal
dma_window must not overlap the APB target window; the timer owns 0x40000000..0x40000fff and the DMA control window is 16 bytes at 0x40003000
